briefing.title: Welcome to Eastgate
briefing.lead: A Chicago-style neighborhood with one big empty building
facts: Saint Wenceslas Church and its parish hall, at Vine and 18th
The hall has been empty since 2019
Five people want to lease it

briefing.title: Saint Wenceslas Church, 1893
briefing.lead: Built by Czech immigrants, the neighborhood's first big wave
facts: The parish hall stands beside it on 18th Street
Czech Mass ended in 1971
Spanish Mass began in 1976

briefing.title: Carved in Czech
briefing.lead: "Kostel sv. Václava" means Church of Saint Wenceslas
facts: The oldest layer on the block, still visible
The Czech families who carved it have mostly moved away
The church and its cornerstone are still here

briefing.title: Language spoken at home
briefing.lead: The same blocks, three different generations
facts: 1950: about 4 in 10 homes spoke Czech
2000: about 7 in 10 homes spoke Spanish
Today: about half Spanish, a growing share English only

briefing.title: The Czech heritage society
briefing.lead: Eleven members, all living in the suburbs
facts: The last Czech business on the block closed in 1994
Members meet once a year
None of them live in Eastgate

briefing.title: Two signs, one wall
briefing.lead: A Spanish tortillería sign painted over an older Czech beer ad
facts: Look closely: the red "PIVO" letters show through
"Pivo" is Czech for beer
Each group left its mark on the same wall

briefing.title: One place, three names
briefing.lead: Who you are decides what you call it
facts: Realtors: the Eastgate Arts District
Longtime neighbors: the Barrio
The heritage society: Little Prague

briefing.title: The women's circle, 1921 to 2019
briefing.lead: Sewing and childcare in the parish hall for 98 years
facts: First in Czech, later in Spanish
It closed when the hall closed in 2019
The same room, the same chairs

briefing.title: The block after dark
briefing.lead: A library survey asked women about this stretch at night
facts: 7 in 10 women avoid the sidewalk by the church after dark
The streetlight by the church is broken
The storefronts on Vine are well lit

briefing.title: Who lives here now
briefing.lead: A walking neighborhood with rents on the rise
facts: Median household income: about $41,000
Rents are up about 40% since 2015
4 in 10 households have no car

briefing.title: Ticketed on the sidewalk
briefing.lead: Fourteen vendors have been cited by the city
facts: They sell elotes, fruit and handmade goods
They have no legal place to sell
Many set up in front of the empty hall

briefing.title: Cultural landscape
briefing.lead: The visible mark people leave on a place
facts: Buildings, signs, languages, businesses, who uses which spaces
Every group adds a layer
Whatever opens here becomes the next layer

mercado.title: Mercado Vine
mercado.lead: Fourteen vendor stalls under one roof in the parish hall
facts: Food, produce, embroidery, a notary
A bulletin board for jobs and rooms
Run by people who already sell on this block

mercado.title: A legal place to sell
mercado.lead: Right now the vendors sell outside and get tickets
facts: 14 vendors cited by the city
The market would move them indoors
Stall rent: $300 a month

mercado.title: How people find work here
mercado.lead: 11 of the 14 vendors are family or neighbors from the same towns
facts: A nephew's first job
A room to rent
A notary who speaks Spanish

mercado.title: Why people stayed
mercado.lead: "Landlords in other neighborhoods would not rent to us"
facts: First: limited choices pushed families here
Now: "we stay because we want to"
"A cushion against the world"

mercado.title: The money
mercado.lead: 14 stalls x $300 a month = $4,200 a month in rent
facts: Cash only, no website
Vendors are already waiting
"Steady money is still money"

mercado.title: Every family leaves a line
mercado.lead: The Spanish sign covers the Czech one
facts: Rosario points to the same wall Dolores showed
Layers of different groups on one building
Her market would add the next layer

brewery.title: Eastgate Brewing
brewery.lead: A taproom inside the old parish hall
facts: Keeps the arched windows and old brick
Copper tanks and long shared tables
Founder grew up on 19th Street

brewery.title: Keeping the cornerstone
brewery.lead: "We keep the front of the building"
facts: The Czech cornerstone stays in place
The signs on the side wall get restored
Old layers stay visible

brewery.title: The beer ad under the sign
brewery.lead: The first beer is a Czech-style pilsner
facts: Named for the Czech beer ad painted on the hall in the 1930s
Ghost Sign Amber, Cornerstone Stout, Vine and Eighteenth Lager
Beers named for real local landmarks

brewery.title: Not his brand
facts: He refuses to sell a beer called "the Barrio"
He uses landmark names instead
He knows the names people use for this place

brewery.title: Local on purpose
facts: Taproom food from the bakery and tortillería
One wall for local artists, rent free
Feedback from neighbors every month

brewery.title: The worry
brewery.lead: Pints at $8 on a street where incomes are about $41,000
facts: Rents are already up 40% since 2015
Neighbors say new places raise prices
First-time owner; the spreadsheet is his brother-in-law's

landing.title: The Landing
landing.lead: Gym, co-working, classes and childcare in the parish hall
facts: The gym and co-working floor are women only
Childcare and classes are open to everyone
A lit, staffed side entrance on 18th Street

landing.title: The Wenceslas Women's Circle
facts: 1921: a sewing room, one of the few public places open to women
The circle met here for 98 years
Women have used this room for generations

landing.title: The Círculo de Mujeres
landing.lead: Her other grandmother sat in the same room
facts: The circle switched from Czech to Spanish
Same room, same chairs, a new group
"Same room, new roles"

landing.title: The block after dark
landing.lead: 7 in 10 women avoid the block by the church at night
facts: The streetlight by the church is broken
Her plan adds a lit, staffed side entrance
Who feels safe here is part of the landscape

landing.title: The nearest daycare
landing.lead: 14 blocks away: 26 minutes with a stroller
facts: 4 in 10 homes here have no car
Childcare at $6 an hour
Memberships at $45 a month

landing.title: The Circle room today
landing.lead: English and Spanish classes, open to everyone
facts: The old women's circle room stays a gathering space
Classes serve the families already here
"An unmet need with a history"

residences.title: The Residences at Vine
residences.lead: Sixty luxury lofts on the corner of Vine and 18th
facts: Six stories of glass and gray panels
A boutique pilates studio and a salad shop
Brand name: SoVine

residences.title: Who could afford it?
facts: That is 70% of Eastgate's median income of $41,000
One-bedrooms from $3,100 a month
Built for people who don't live here yet

residences.title: What comes down
residences.lead: The demolition permit is already filed
facts: The 1893 church and its Czech cornerstone
The parish hall and its two painted signs
130 years of layers on one corner

residences.title: The heritage nod
residences.lead: Three salvaged bricks and a plaque in the lobby
facts: Everything else on the site is demolished
No church, no hall, no signs
"Authentic luxury"

residences.title: Traction
facts: Reserved by people who don't live here yet
Rents in Eastgate are up 40% since 2015
A sign that newcomers are arriving

residences.title: Community engagement
residences.lead: One flyer with a QR code
facts: He will skip the community meeting
Residents are "the existing demographic"
Close, demolish, deliver in 18 months

littleprague.title: Little Prague Experience
littleprague.lead: A themed beer hall and gift shop in the parish hall
facts: Pretzels, strudel and an oompah band
Gerry plays the accordion
Menus in Czech, English on the back

littleprague.title: Is that Czech?
littleprague.lead: Lederhosen, feathered hats and cuckoo clocks
facts: Lederhosen and alpine hats come from Bavaria and the Alps
Cuckoo clocks come from Germany's Black Forest
"It's all basically the same thing"

littleprague.title: Market research
littleprague.lead: 9 of 11 heritage society members said yes
facts: All 11 live in the suburbs
No one who lives in Eastgate was asked
"I did the math. I think."

littleprague.title: Renaming the street
facts: "Little Prague" is the heritage society's name
Neighbors call it the Barrio
He is sure the neighbors will love it

littleprague.title: Painting over the sign
littleprague.lead: A Czech flag over the Spanish sign
facts: The Spanish sign has covered the Czech ad since the 1980s
His plan erases the newer layer
"It was kind of faded anyway"

littleprague.title: Where the customers come from
littleprague.lead: Tour buses from the suburbs, 40 people a bus
facts: Eventually
4 in 10 Eastgate homes have no car
His customers would not be the neighbors
